headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra can write and egress broadly while social-auto-upload can push account-bound media, creating default-path data, conflict, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and pass stdin/stdout, while social-auto-upload operates on local media/account files; a prompt-injection path exists only if an operator manually bridges outputs into inputs. No shared channel is documented, so the interaction is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Kestra-generated text into social-auto-upload captions or prompts
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted workspace files
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for workflow artifacts and upload assets
Require manual review before copying any generated text into upload metadata
Use a read-only handoff file for captions
Add a short allowlist for fields that may be transferred between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress; social-auto-upload handles account data and media. If they share a workspace or account files, sensitive workflow data can flow into upload-side outputs or third-party APIs in default use.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same filesystem directory
IF Kestra artifacts contain secrets, database rows, or messages that are later packaged by social-auto-upload
mitigations: Store upload assets and orchestration artifacts in separate directories
Redact secrets from Kestra logs before handoff
Disable automatic inclusion of arbitrary files in upload jobs
Review outbound requests from both agents for sensitive payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; social-auto-upload cannot write files but does support multiple instances with one account file per session. Conflict is plausible around shared account files or shared directories, though not as severe as dual unrestricted writers because B lacks write capability.
conditions: IF both agents target the same account file or upload directory
IF Kestra runs concurrent workflows that mutate files consumed by social-auto-upload
mitigations: Assign one account file per social-auto-upload session
Serialize writes to any shared directory
Place Kestra outputs in a separate staging folder
Use file locks or a single-writer convention

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs and notifications, and social-auto-upload can act on media/account data. If Kestra-produced artifacts are treated as authoritative inputs, social-auto-upload may publish or upload incorrect content without a verification step. The pair lacks documented cross-checking, so the cascade is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes Kestra-produced files or metadata without validation
IF Kestra emits malformed or stale artifacts that are later uploaded
mitigations: Insert a checksum or schema validation step between agents
Require human approval before upload execution
Compare generated metadata against source files
Fail closed on missing or unexpected fields

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra can process logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but the pair can still create compliance gaps if regulated data is routed into the upload agent. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data such as personal messages or database records are included in Kestra workflows
IF social-auto-upload is used on data subject to retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to the upload agent
Exclude regulated records from workflow inputs
Document retention for account files and media
Add a manual compliance check for each upload batch
